q: A SaaS company starts the month with $20 million of MRR and loses $5 million of it to churn; what is its gross revenue churn?
explain: Gross revenue churn divides the MRR lost by the MRR at the start of the period (ignoring expansion), so $5m ÷ $20m = 25%.

sources.title: Revenue Churn | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: Gross Revenue Churn = Churned MRR ÷ Beginning MRR For example, if a SaaS company with $20 million in MRR lost $5 million in that specific month, the gross churn is 25%.

sources.title: Revenue churn (net and gross revenue churn rate) | ChartMogul
sources.quote: To calculate gross revenue churn, sum up your churn and contraction MRR and divide it by MRR at the start of the same period.

q: A SaaS company with $20 million of beginning MRR loses $5 million to churn but adds $3 million of expansion MRR; what is its net revenue churn?
explain: Net revenue churn subtracts expansion MRR from lost MRR before dividing by beginning MRR: ($5m − $3m) ÷ $20m = 10%.
hook: Net churn nets expansion against losses.

sources.title: Revenue Churn | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: Net Revenue Churn = (Churned MRR – Expansion MRR) ÷ Beginning MRR Continuing from the previous example, let’s say that the SaaS company was able to bring in $3 million in expansion revenue. In that case, the net churn is 10% instead of the 25% gross churn.

sources.title: Study up on churn rate basics to set customer and revenue benchmarks | TechCrunch
sources.quote: Net MRR churn rate — (sum of churn and contraction MRR – sum of expansion an reactivation MRR) / (MRR at start of period).

q: Below what magic number did Scale Venture Partners say a company still has not figured out its model?
explain: Scale's original guidance: above 1x is a compelling investment, below 0.5x means the model is not yet working; CFI likewise advises against further sales and marketing investment below 0.50.

sources.title: Insights | ScaleVP | Magic Number Math
sources.quote: A result greater than 1x, has proven to be a compelling business investment, a result below .5x is a company that still has not figured out it’s model, and a result in between, is a deal that will probably get to success and cashflow breakeven but only in a relatively capital in-efficient way.

sources.title: The SaaS Magic Number: A Guide to Calculation and Analysis | CFI
sources.quote: If the SaaS Magic Number is below 0.50, the company should generally avoid further investment in sales and marketing costs and explore other actions.
